search_strategy: Systematic bulk-dump-then-grep: the agent listed all Mattermost channels, downloaded every channel's full post history to /tmp/chat/*.txt (fixing a literal-\n-vs-newline bug it noticed along the way), then ran repeated 'grep -n' passes for domain terms (ledger, reason, checkpoint, warmup, total_steps, dataset_signature, CHECKPOINT_NAME_TEMPLATE) with file:line output, and finally read the surrounding 15-40 lines of each hit region to get full multi-turn exchanges. It explicitly recognized superseded Jan decisions ('Jan decisions superseded by March/April') and re-derived numeric constants (5.5e-05, MIN_LR_RATIO=0.1, ten-example -> 3-step run) by cross-checking them against its own formula before writing code. It did not appear to touch the wiki (BookStack) or mail (IMAP) at all in the regions sampled -- all 43 surfaced remarks in this run came from Mattermost chat, which matches the corpus (all 47 g11 remarks are chat-only per the answer key), so this was not a missed surface. Its one weakness: several grep passes searched for concept words ('reason', 'warmup', 'checkpoint') that happened to miss threads keyed on different vocabulary (e.g. the '663' PR-review thread never matched any of its query terms), so a handful of remarks were never opened even though the channels containing them were fully downloaded.
end_reason: Run completed normally: branch pushed, PR #737 opened and merged to main (line 9006-9163), CI green, release deployed via git push trigger (Gitea Actions). task_complete=true issued only after confirming merge + CI status (line 9521).
notable: The single lost fact (g11.r2.rule) traces to exactly one un-surfaced remark, g11.r2.l10, which is the ONLY remark in the whole 47-remark set that states min_lr_ratio must be keyword-only; no herring, no other clue, and no ticket text carries that detail, so its absence is a clean not_found rather than a corpus contradiction (line 5039, 6151-6159).

Both r1 herrings and both r2 herrings were found, correctly identified as superseded, and never followed in the shipped code -- the agent explicitly reasoned 'Jan decisions superseded by March/April' (line 4157) and 'later revision' (line 3503) before writing anything.

Despite pointer-sheet 'not found' on 8 remarks (r1.l19, r1.l5, r2.l9, r2.say20, r2.l11, r2.say19, r2.l14, r2.l10), only r2.l10 actually cost a fact -- the other 7 were redundant with remarks the agent did find (verified by grep: none of their distinctive phrases appear anywhere in the transcript).

The agent cross-validated its reconstructed learning-rate formula against the corpus's own stated numeric fixtures before implementing (line 3654, 3704), which is why the observability and exclusions facts for r2 passed cleanly even with several individual clues missing.
